scenarios.name: resnet-transfer-learning-modern-api
scenarios.rationale: B hits nearly every rubric item (ResNet50_Weights.DEFAULT, frozen backbone with new 12-way Linear fc, zero_grad/backward/step, bfloat16 autocast, single cuda.is_available() device check), whereas A uses IMAGENET1K_V2 rather than DEFAULT, wraps fc in Sequential with Dropout, unfreezes the backbone after 3 epochs, uses float16 autocast with GradScaler instead of bfloat16, and enables AMP only on CUDA with a multi-way device check.

scenarios.name: bert-sentiment-onnx-export
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric closely: eval(), torch.onnx.export with dynamo=True, input_ids and attention_mask with input_names, torch.export.export first, dynamic_shapes, and a warning against torch.jit. B uses the legacy exporter with dynamic_axes as its main path, only mentions dynamo as a late fallback, doesn't say to run torch.export.export first, and recommends torch.jit.script as a fallback, which contradicts the rubric.

scenarios.name: safe-checkpoint-save-load-and-quantize
scenarios.rationale: B hits every rubric point (state_dict, weights_only=True with map_location, warning against weights_only=False, torchao quantize_, torch.ao being phased out) but gives no concrete INT8 config, while A recommends safetensors and demos torch.ao.quantize_dynamic as option 1, never states the weights_only=False risk, and only hedges on the torch.ao deprecation, though it does show torchao quantize_ with INT8 configs.
